problem: Deep RL agents (LSTM, episodic-memory agents such as MERLIN/MRA) need many episodes to explore and learn models of a new environment. They explore within a task but do not plan over gathered knowledge, so they cannot reuse it for later tasks in the same novel environment.
motivation: A deployed agent, e.g. a household robot, should be useful immediately and improve as it gains experience in a new environment, exploring while solving tasks and reusing what it learns. The authors observe that prior memory agents only match a 'within-task optimal exploration' baseline, and hypothesize that a weighted sum of retrieved memories followed by an MLP is not expressive enough to support planning.
key_idea: Episodic Planning Networks (EPNs) replace the weighted-sum-plus-MLP memory readout with iterated, parameter-shared self-attention over episodic memories (conditioned on the goal, with the current state appended only at the end), enabling meta-learned value-iteration-like planning within a single episode.
insight: Episodic memory alone (MERLIN/MRA) helps only slightly over LSTM; the self-attention planner is what yields planning, and a single attention iteration is not enough (Fig. 4a: performance improves with 1→2→4 iterations). Decoding distance-to-goal from the planner output improves with more iterations and spreads radially from the goal (Fig. 4c,d), even beyond the iteration count used in training, which is evidence of a value-iteration-like algorithm. Because planning is learned, it generalizes to larger maps (7 and 9 intersections) than seen in training.
method: RTS problem formulation: meta-RL generalization where an environment is sampled per episode and a sequence of tasks (new start/goal, i.e. reward functions) is sampled within it; objective E_e E_r J_{e,r}

Episodic memory: each timestep writes a transition memory (concat of embeddings of current observation, previous action, previous observation); the current goal embedding is appended to every slot before planning

Planner: iterated self-attention B_{i+1}=f(B_i+MHA(LayerNorm(B_i))) with shared parameters across iterations (f = ReLU + 2-layer MLP, 64-d, 1-4 heads); current state is appended only after the final iteration, followed by a shared MLP and a feature-wise max pool

Policy network: 2-layer MLP over planner output plus state-goal embedding skip connection, producing policy logits and a value baseline; trained with actor-critic (IMPALA/V-trace, 1000 actors, TPU learner); pixel inputs use a small 3-layer residual conv net

Nxk scalable variant: k most recent memories act as the belief state and attend to the full memory, then self-attend, giving linear cost in memory size; with k=50 it recovers 92% of the A2A performance

Benchmarks: Memory&Planning Game (4x4 symbol grid, 100 steps/episode) and One-Shot StreetLearn (StreetView neighborhoods with 5 intersections, degree-2 nodes removed, 200 steps/episode, turn left/right/forward, 12 training cities, held-out Paris South-East)

setting.backbone: EPN (iterated self-attention planner + MLP policy, small residual conv encoder) trained from scratch with IMPALA actor-critic
setting.model_size: small (64-d embeddings, 64-unit MLPs, 1-4 attention heads; 16/32/32-channel conv layers)
setting.training_data: Meta-RL from scratch on procedurally sampled environments: random symbol grids; StreetLearn neighborhoods (5 intersections) from 12 European cities, ~3-4e9 environment steps
setting.observation: state image + goal image (StreetLearn, from StreetView frames), or symbol IDs (Memory&Planning Game); no other information
setting.action_space: StreetLearn: turn left / turn right / move forward on a discrete graph; Memory&Planning Game: left/right/up/down/collect
setting.simulator: StreetLearn (Google StreetView graph and images); custom Memory&Planning Game

numbers.eval_set_note: held-out city region (Paris South-East), 5-intersection neighborhoods, averaged over 100 consecutive episodes
numbers.extra: trained on 5-intersection neighborhoods of 12 cities, evaluated on a held-out city; 200 steps/episode; fraction of oracle measured in last third of episode
numbers.evidence: "successfully reaching 28.7 goals per episode (averaged over 100 consecutive episodes, Figure 3c)"; "EPNs achieve on average 88% ± 2% of the performance of an oracle"

numbers_note: Not a standard navigation benchmark; results are mostly in figures. Memory&Planning Game numbers only appear in figures. Baselines: Merlin/MRA up to 14.5 goals per episode, LSTM 10.0.
results: On One-Shot StreetLearn the EPN reaches 28.7 goals per episode on held-out-city neighborhoods, versus at most 14.5 for the best baselines (Merlin/MRA) and 10.0 for the LSTM. It reaches 88% ± 2% of oracle performance in the last third of episodes and matches the shortest-path optimum after 10-15 tasks. It generalizes to 7- and 9-intersection maps and reaches near-oracle performance in the Memory&Planning Game.
limitations: Self-attention over all memories scales quadratically with episode length; the linear Nxk variant loses about 8% of performance
Evaluated only on simplified graph-like domains: degree-2 nodes removed in StreetLearn, small maps of 5-12 intersections, and no real-robot or continuous-control tests
Trained with billions of RL steps from scratch; temporally abstract (jumpy) planning and planning over belief states are left to future work
